target: На втором этаже нашего дома находится библиотека.
english: The library is on the second floor of our building.
tip: For location, На (na = on) takes the prepositional case: втором этаже (vtorom etazhe = second floor), not the base form этаж (etazh).

english: A third of the students were late.
tip: With a fraction like Треть (tret = a third), the verb stays singular: опоздала (opozdala = was late), never plural.

english: The ticket costs five hundred rubles.
tip: Numbers from five up take the genitive plural: пятьсот (pyatsot = five hundred) рублей (rubley = of rubles), not рубли (rubli).

english: I want four pieces of cake.
tip: Numbers two, three, four take the genitive singular, not plural: четыре кусочка (chetyre kusochka = four pieces), not кусочки (kusochki).

english: One of the students didn't come.
tip: Один из (odin iz = one of) is followed by the genitive plural: студентов (studentov = of students).

english: These rules are followed by all employees.
tip: A reflexive passive uses -ся (sya): соблюдаются (soblyudayutsya = are followed). The doer takes the instrumental: сотрудниками (sotrudnikami = by staff).

english: It is known that he is a good specialist.
tip: Известно (izvestno = it is known) is an impersonal neuter form with no subject, followed by что (chto = that) and a clause.

target: Эта улица названа в честь поэта.
english: This street is named after a poet.
tip: В честь (v chest = in honor of) takes the genitive: поэта (poeta = of the poet). It is how Russian says named after someone.

english: The postman delivers the letters.
tip: Case, not position, marks roles, so the object can come first: Письма (pisma = letters) is the object, почтальон (pochtalyon = postman) the subject.

english: You look great!
tip: выглядишь (vyglyadish = you look) takes an adverb, not an adjective: классно (klassno = great) is the -о adverb form.

english: The salary is fifty thousand.
tip: Russian drops the verb to be in the present; a dash links Зарплата (zarplata = salary) and пятьдесят (pyatdesyat = fifty).

english: March eighth is a holiday.
tip: In dates the month goes genitive: марта (marta = of March), so Восьмое марта (vosmoye marta) reads the eighth of March.

english: He runs every other day.
tip: через (cherez) plus a time word means every other one: через день (cherez den) = every other day, not daily.

english: He lives on the third floor.
tip: Floors take на plus the prepositional: на третьем этаже (na tretyem etazhe = on the third floor), never в (v).

target: Площадь, на которой стоит памятник, красивая.
english: The square on which the monument stands is beautiful.
tip: который (kotory) changes gender to match its noun: Площадь (ploshchad) is feminine, so на которой (na kotoroy = on which) is feminine.

target: Тише ты, ребёнок спит в соседней комнате!
english: Quiet down, the child is sleeping in the next room!
tip: Тише (tishe = quieter) is the comparative of тихо (tikho = quietly), used alone as a command to be quiet.

target: Моя дочь перешла в пятый класс этой осенью.
english: My daughter moved to fifth grade this autumn.
tip: Moving up a grade uses в plus the accusative: перешла в пятый класс (pereshla v pyaty klass = moved into fifth grade).

english: Give half a kilo of cheese.
tip: Quantity words push the next noun to genitive: полкило сыра (polkilo syra = half a kilo of cheese), not сыр (syr).

english: The sixth lesson is the most difficult.
tip: самый (samy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative: самый сложный (samy slozhny = the most difficult).

english: There are a thousand rubles in the account.
tip: Some masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the prepositional after на (na): счету (schetu), from счёт (schet = account).

english: The temperature is minus ten degrees.
tip: After десять (desyat = ten) the noun turns genitive plural: десять градусов (desyat gradusov = ten degrees).

english: Hundreds of people came to the concert.
tip: люди (lyudi) has an irregular genitive plural людей (lyudey = of people), used after Сотни (sotni = hundreds).

target: Через пять лет он окончит университет.
english: In five years he will graduate from university.
tip: Через (cherez) plus the accusative marks a future point: пять лет (pyat let = five years) counts forward from now.

target: Можно вас спросить, как пройти к ближайшему метро?
english: May I ask you how to get to the nearest metro?
tip: метро (metro) never changes form; к ближайшему (k blizhayshemu = to the nearest) shows dative, but метро stays fixed.

target: Не могли бы вы подождать несколько минут в коридоре?
english: Could you wait a few minutes in the corridor?
tip: бы makes a request polite and tentative: не могли бы вы (ne mogli by vy = could you) is softer than plain можете (mozhete).

english: Thanks for writing (informal)!
tip: Спасибо, что (spasibo, chto) plus a past-tense verb means thanks for doing something: написал (napisal = wrote).

english: It's good that you called.
tip: Хорошо, что (khorosho, chto = good that) opens a clause giving the reason you are glad: ты позвонил (ty pozvonil = you called).

target: Она накопила денег, чтобы поехать в путешествие.
english: She saved money to go on a trip.
tip: накопила денег (nakopila deneg) puts деньги (dengi = money) into genitive to mean saved some money, an unspecified amount, not a named sum.

target: Или мы идём сейчас, или остаёмся дома.
english: Either we go now, or we stay home.
tip: Paired Или... или (ili... ili = either... or) marks the two choices: идём (idyom = we go) or остаёмся (ostayomsya = we stay).

target: Нет сомнений в том, что он прав.
english: There is no doubt that he is right.
tip: After Нет (net = there is no) the noun goes genitive: сомнений (somneniy = doubts), never nominative сомнения (somneniya).
